kind.description: concept carries one step of the explanation, in the order a reader needs them. misconception is the section that stops to name the wrong turn most readers take here, before the article goes on.

prose.description: One paragraph of the article. It carries the teaching on its own; nothing else on this section is required.

note.description: A short aside in the margin: a definition, a unit, a caveat, a number worth having. Omit it unless the margin genuinely earns it. Most sections have none.

figure.description: A graph, when a relationship is easier to see than to read. Best where one quantity varies with another and the shape of that variation is the point. Include one where the subject genuinely has such a relationship, and none at all where it does not — a topic with nothing to plot should have no figure rather than an invented one.

shape.description: The family of function to draw. turning: A curve with exactly one turning point. Exactly 4: h, k, xr, yr. The turning point is at x = h, where y = k. The curve also passes through (xr, yr), a second real value from elsewhere in the range: xr must not equal h, and yr must be the value the curve genuinely takes at xr, which is never the same as k. Whether the curve peaks or dips is WORKED OUT from those two points — there is no direction to choose. Use this whenever the figure is about where something is highest or lowest. polynomial: c0 + c1*x + c2*x^2 + ... — 2 to 6 coefficients, lowest power first. Straight lines and general curves. If the figure is about a maximum or a minimum, use quadratic instead. exponential: a*e^(b*x) + c — exactly 3: a, b, c. Growth and decay. logarithmic: a*ln(b*x) + c — exactly 3: a, b, c. Only defined where b*x > 0. sinusoidal: a*sin(b*x + c) + d — exactly 4: a, b, c, d. Waves and oscillation. power: a*x^b + c — exactly 3: a, b, c. Square laws, inverse squares. reciprocal: a/(b*x) + c — exactly 3: a, b, c. Undefined at x = 0.

coefficients.description: The coefficients for the chosen shape, in the order its description gives. The count must match that shape exactly. Before settling on them, check two things: that the curve they produce really has the shape the caption claims, and that its values are plausible in the unit named by y_label.

domain.description: The x range to draw, as [min, max]. min must be smaller than max. Choose a range where the interesting behaviour is visible.

x_label.description: What the horizontal axis measures, with its unit.

y_label.description: What the vertical axis measures, with its unit.

caption.description: One sentence saying what the diagram shows. Not a restatement of the axis labels.

marks.description: x positions worth pointing at, inside the domain. The runtime labels each with the coordinate the function actually has there, so do not describe them. Usually empty or one.

ask_line.description: The closing line of the article, after the last section. Land what was worked out, then ask where the reader wants to go next. It must end in a question.
